questions.question: A.B and C are assigned to complete a work. If the ratio of time taken by A, B and C is 4 ∶ 3 ∶ 6. Find the ratio of their efficiency.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time.

Given Time Ratio of A, B, and C = 4 : 3 : 6

Efficiency Ratio = 1/4 : 1/3 : 1/6

Multiply by LCM of (4, 3, 6) i.e., 12 ⇒ (1/4 × 12) : (1/3 × 12) : (1/6 × 12)

Efficiency Ratio = 3 : 4 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4 : 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of time taken by A, B, and C = 4 : 3 : 6

**Concept Used:**

Let the time taken by A, B, and C be 4 days, 3 days, and 6 days respectively.

Total work = LCM of Time Taken

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A

 12 ÷ 4 = 3

 12 ÷ 3 = 4

⇒ Efficiency of A = 3

⇒ Efficiency of B = 4

⇒ Efficiency of C = 2

⇒ Ratio of their efficiency = 3 : 4 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 4 : 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of time taken by two individuals is x : y, then the ratio of their efficiencies will be y : x.

Total Work Formula

Total Work = Efficiency × Time taken. This implies a person with higher efficiency takes less time to complete the same work.

Combined Work

If person A completes a work in 'a' days and person B completes it in 'b' days, their combined efficiency is (1/a + 1/b), and the total time taken is (a × b) ÷ (a + b) days.

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows a discount of 20% on the marked price and still gains 12% on the whole. Find at what percent above the cost price did he mark his goods?
questions.solution:
Given:

Discount = 20%

Profit = 12%

Formula Used:

Selling price = Cost price + Profit 

Selling price = Marked price – Discount

Calculation:

Let the cost price be Rs. ‘x’

Profit = 12% of x

⇒ 0.12x

Selling price = Cost price + Profit 

⇒ x + 0.12x

⇒ 1.12x

Now,

Selling price = Marked price – Discount

⇒ 1.12x = MP – 20% of MP

⇒ 1.12x = MP – (1/5)MP

⇒ 1.12x = (4/5)MP

⇒ MP = 5 × 1.12x/4

⇒ MP = 1.4x

⇒ MP = x + 40% of x

∴ The market price should be 40% above the cost price.

Alternate Method:

Relationship between Cost price and Marked price

CP : MP = (100 – Discount) : (100 + Profit)

⇒ (100 – 20) : (100 + 12)

⇒ 80: 112

⇒ 5: 7

Required percentage = [(7 – 5)/5] × 100

⇒ 2 × 100/5

⇒ 40%

∴ The market price should be 40% above the cost price

questions.question: In how many least number of complete years will a sum of money become more than four times of itself at the rate of 14 percent per annum on simple interest?

Amount = P + SI

questions.question: Two stations A and B are 230 km apart on a straight line. One train starts from A at 4 a.m. and travels towards B at 40 km/hr. Another train starts from B at 5 a.m. and travels towards A at a speed of 55 km/hr. At what time will they meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance covered by **Train 1** from 4 a.m. to 5 a.m. = 40 km/hr × 1 hr = 40 km.

Remaining distance at 5 a.m. = 230 − 40 = 190 km.

**Relative speed** (opposite directions) = 40 + 55 = 95 km/hr.

Time to meet from 5 a.m. = 190 ÷ 95 = 2 hours.

Meeting time = 5 a.m. + 2 hours = 7 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd83e302b983813ce045a7a126ec7541d07e369e5fb2f103f02b2b67537170b4.png] 

**Given:**

Total distance between **Station A** and **Station B** = 230 km.

Speed of **Train A** = 40 km/hr (starts at 4 a.m.).

Speed of **Train B** = 55 km/hr (starts at 5 a.m.).

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, we make the start time of both trains the same (5 a.m.).

⇒ Distance covered by **Train A** in 1 hour (from 4 to 5 a.m.) = Speed × Time = 40 × 1 = 40 km.

⇒ Remaining Distance to be covered after 5 a.m. = 230 − 40 = 190 km.

⇒ Since trains are moving in **opposite directions**, Relative Speed = SA + SB

⇒ Relative Speed = 40 + 55 = 95 km/hr.

⇒ Time taken to meet = Remaining Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time taken = 190 ÷ 95 = 2 hours.

⇒ Meeting Time = 5 a.m. + 2 hours = 7 a.m.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Same Direction Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the **difference** of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂.

Time of Meeting

To calculate the **Meeting Time**, the distance between the objects must be considered from the point in time when both objects start moving simultaneously.</p

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 500 becomes Rs. 580 at simple interest in 2 years. In how many years will the sum of Rs. 650 amounts to Rs. 858 at the same rate of simple interest?
questions.solution:
Given:

Principle = Rs. 500

Amount = Rs. 580

Time = 2 years

Formula used:

S.I = Amount – P

S.I = (P × R × T)/100

Where S.I = Simple Interest

P = Principal, R = Rate, T = time

Calculation:

S.I = 580 – 500 = 80

⇒ 80 = (500 × R × 2)/100

⇒ R = 8%

As per the question,

S.I = 858 – 650 = 208

⇒ 208 = (650 × 8 × T)/100

⇒ T = 4 years.

∴ The time is 4 years.

questions.question: There is a rectangular garden of 150 metres × 25 metres, A path of width 10 metres is built around the garden. What is the area of the path?
questions.solution:
GIVEN:

Width of the path = 10 meter

Dimensions of rectangular garden = 150 m × 25 m

FORMULA USED:

Area of rectangle = Length × Breadth

CALCULATION:

Length of smaller rectangle (Only park) = 150 m

Breadth of smaller rectangle (Only park) = 25 m

And

Length of larger rectangle (Including street) = 150 + 10 + 10 = 170 m

Breadth of larger rectangle (Including street) = 25 + 10 + 10 = 45 m

Hence,

Area of street = (170 × 45) – (150 × 25) = 7650 – 3750 = 3900 m²

**The answer is 3900 m²**

__Short Trick__

Area of path = 2w (l + b + 2w)

Where ‘w’ is the width of path and ‘b’ is the width of rectangular garden, ‘l’ is the length of rectangular garden.

So,

Area of path = 2 × 10 × (150 + 25 + 2 × 10) = 3900 m²
